summary.name: Hammerspoon
summary.one_liner: Hammerspoon is a macOS automation tool that bridges the operating system to a Lua scripting engine, letting you script windows, apps, devices, and events.
use_cases: Bind keyboard shortcuts to window operations
Run commands when wifi connects to a home network
Show alerts when battery drops below a set level
Trigger actions based on location or system events
Automate interactions with macOS apps and filesystem
summary.what_it_does: Hammerspoon is a bridge between macOS and a Lua scripting engine. Its extensions expose system functionality such as applications, windows, mouse pointers, filesystem objects, audio devices, batteries, screens, low-level keyboard and mouse events, clipboards, location services, and wifi. Users write a Lua configuration file (~/.hammerspoon/init.lua) that connects events to actions. Pre-made plugins called Spoons are available, and the project has API documentation and a Getting Started Guide. Out of the box it does nothing until a script is written.
notable: Lua scripting engine as the core, with extensions exposing macOS APIs
Extensible via pure Lua scripts or Objective-C extensions
Listed on awesome-mac as open source and freeware
caveats: Does nothing out of the box; requires writing Lua configuration
Older Macs may need an older release from the Release Notes
